verdict: JPMorgan earned $13.0B in the quarter — revenue rose 7% to $45.8B, but credit costs jumped 77% to $4.7B as the bank built a $2.2B reserve for the Apple card portfolio it has agreed to take over, pulling profit down 7% from a year ago.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: reported basis, vs a year ago

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus the interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine, up 7% on higher deposit balances and more revolving card balances, partly offset by lower rates.

segments.name: Noninterest revenue
segments.note: Fees, trading and asset-management income — up 7%, with Markets revenue up 17% to $8.2B and asset management fees up 17%.

opex.name: Compensation expense
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's workforce — its biggest cost.

opex.name: Technology, communications & equipment
opex.note: Technology, telecoms and equipment as the bank invests in AI and its platforms.

opex.name: Occupancy & other expense
opex.note: Branches and offices ($1,475M of occupancy) plus other general costs ($1,676M).

takeaways.title: Returns still lead the industry
takeaways.text: Return on tangible common equity was 18% (15% on common equity) — profitability far beyond what other big banks produce, on $13.0B of net income.

takeaways.title: Markets had a strong quarter
takeaways.text: Markets revenue rose 17% YoY to $8.2B and asset management fees rose 17%, helping total revenue grow 7% even as card income fell.

takeaways.title: Credit costs spiked — on purpose
takeaways.text: The provision for credit losses jumped 77% YoY to $4.7B, but $2.2B of it was a reserve built ahead of taking over the Apple credit card portfolio — setting money aside early, not loans going bad today. Actual net charge-offs were $2.5B.

oneTimers: The $4.7B provision for credit losses includes a net reserve build of $2.1B, reflecting a $2.2B reserve established for the forward purchase commitment of the Apple credit card portfolio — money set aside before the portfolio arrives, not losses on loans already made.
follow100Note: JPMorgan reports revenue two ways: $45.8B reported (GAAP), used here, or $46.8B on a 'managed' basis that grosses up tax-exempt income. Net income is identical either way.
footerNote: JPMorgan headlines 'managed' revenue of $46.8B; this page uses reported (GAAP) revenue of $45.8B — the difference is a tax gross-up that does not change net income. For a bank, credit costs (the provision for credit losses) play the role of cost of revenue, and 'operating profit' here is income before income taxes.
costNodePlain: Money set aside for loans that may not be repaid — the provision for credit losses: $2.5B of loans were charged off in the quarter and $2.1B was added to reserves, reflecting a $2.2B reserve for the Apple card portfolio JPMorgan has agreed to take over.
